items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I worked with Jo ten, eleven years. Actually, I worked with Jo twelve years

ctx.x: That's when they were having the festival. Well, I played there the first night with Benny Goodman's big band. That was in '58. And, of course, John had made us stay over to play for Billie and me and Pee-wee and Jack T., Georgie Auld and Prez and Buck, Jo Jones. I don't remember who -- Walter Page. That was the rhythm section. I don't remember who we had on piano. So we all stayed there and played for -- I stayed -- as a matter of fact, I did two days, you know. I stayed there and did the -- after Benny's…

So Prez was -- he was sick then. It was getting to him, you know, he was really failing. He was short-winded, he didn't have any stamina, couldn't hardly fill his horn, you know what I mean? Sound -- couldn't control his sound. So that day, we had a rehearsal, rehearsing things with Billie. So George and I was always tight, you know? items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Buddy Rich loved him, Jo Jones loved him, all the drummers knew about A.G. Godley.

ctx.x: A question I wanted to ask you is, you know Basie has been quoted as saying that his band was developed from the rhythm section, and then up through the tenor sax positions, and then to the rest of the band.

Yeah he loved tenors. You see in those days, you only had one tenor player, featured tenor player, but he always had two so he started out with Herschel and Lester. So he had two of the world’s greatest and wasn’t nobody — he had to make it. So when they went to New York they just chopped everybody down. And that rhythm section, he had Walt Page, Jo Jones, because that was all the American rhythm section, and himself, Freddie Green. That was quite a band.

I wanted to ask you about that particular sound. There were different sounds, they say a different feel to the music that there was in the southwest than on the west coast or in the New York scene. Could you describe for us how you felt the sound of the Basie band was different? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
